summary: The timer broadcasts through the ordinary active Actor list and concrete class descriptors into synchronous BDX event10. claims.Finding: Event execution calls the native BDX interpreter synchronously with the current bank table. UpdateTree may recurse into child VM contexts; normal completion marks the context and decrements Actor+1464 once.3E1840 restores the two ambient VM globals before destroying the temporary VM. Destruction can execute a nonzero cleanup PC through BDX, recursively tears down children, frees stack buffers, decrements Work refs and balances the Actor count if not already complete. A suspended/yielded temporary VM is still destroyed before this handler returns; no persistence of this temporary context is shown. Native traps can have effects outside this bounded closure.
claims.Limitations: Static original-build evidence. No live timer firing, script execution, concurrent-writer census or all-class/all-path completeness proof.

claims.Finding: No lock, generation token or pin is present in the checked list iterator/broadcaster/inserter/drainer bodies. Broadcast returns to the current Actor's link after arbitrary BDX; the concrete stack therefore depends on the current Actor, descriptor, Script/Work/owner binding and allocator remaining valid until the native operation finishes. Existing App-task provenance shows caller context but does not prove exclusive OS-thread ownership, worker quiescence, or safety against a reentrant disposal/bulk teardown. A trainer must obtain a separately proven stable execution/lifetime boundary before read-modify-restore transactions.
claims.Limitations: Static original-build evidence. No live timer firing, script execution, concurrent-writer census or all-class/all-path completeness proof.
